previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted with right flank pain and diagnosed with an obstructing right ureteral stone causing pyelonephritis and E. coli bacteremia leading to sepsis. His hospital course was complicated by three episodes of sustained ventricular tachycardia requiring ICD shocks, likely triggered by the infection. He was treated with IV ceftriaxone, and a ureteral stent was placed to relieve obstruction. He developed C. difficile colitis, managed with oral vancomycin. His heart function declined, with a new echo showing LVEF 35–40%, and he was uptitrated on metoprolol after refusing amiodarone due to prior liver issues. His torsemide was held due to hypovolemia from infection and diarrhea. He stabilized, completed treatment, and was discharged to extended care for continued IV antibiotics and monitoring.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ man with h/o CAD s/p MI and DESx2 to RCA

ACTIVE ISSUES
===============
#Chest pain: Patient with ongoing episodes of chest pain that do 
not correlate with EKG changes concerning for ischemia, no 
troponin leak.  The palpitations associated with his chest pain 
have appeared to be PVCs by telemetry.  Patient underwent 
Persantine Mibi which was negative for any acute ischemic 
changes.  Given his high PVC burden, EP was asked to see patient 
and made some adjustments to his pacemaker settings, allowing 
for greater AV delay prior to RV pacing.  Patient was resistant 
to taking both Metoprolol and Lisinopril given low systolic 
blood pressures so his Lisinopril was held and he was encouraged 
to be compliant with Metoprolol administration.  At time of 
discharge, patient reported improvement in his overall symptoms 
after adjustments made on his pacemaker and more consistent 
adherence to Metoprolol dosing.

admission ___. C diff returned positive on ___ so patient 
started PO vanc and was scheduled to receive 2 weeks post
